text:
tori: Hi folks, quick onboarding snag. I'm on macOS Ventura (M2) and our dev compose starts postgres but my local psql client can't connect using localhost:5432. I get 'could not connect to server: Connection refused'.

jake: Welcome! Are you running the app/psql on the host or inside a WSL-like env? On mac it's usually host -> localhost:5432 should work if the container publishes the port.

tori: Host. `docker ps` shows `0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp`. I can `docker exec -it db pg_isready` and it says accepting connections.

infra-bot: infra-bot posted: "container postgres-db restarted (exit code 1) 2 times in last 10m"

cia: small thought: do you have a local postgres installed (Homebrew) that's listening on 5432 already? try `lsof -i :5432`

tori: lsof shows nothing. I tried `ps aux | grep postgres` and only the container process is running.

jake: Could be the new socket vs tcp nuance: libpq tries unix socket before TCP when host is omitted. Try `psql -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres` explicitly forcing TCP.

tori: good idea — forcing `-h localhost` still yields connection refused. `telnet localhost 5432` fails but `docker exec -it db ss -ltn` shows LISTEN on 0.0.0.0:5432.

nia: Is your firewall blocking Docker's NAT? Also if you use Podman or colima, networking behaves differently. Which engine is Docker Desktop or colima?

tori: Docker Desktop. Firewall is off. I also have colima installed but not running.

lee: On M1/M2 macs some folks run compose with `network_mode: host` (not supported on Mac), which confuses things. Another angle: Are you using a socket path in .psqlrc or PGHOST env? `echo $PGHOST`

tori: PGHOST was unset. .psqlrc doesn't set host. Weirdly, `nc -zv $(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' db) 5432` from host fails because that IP is internal to the Docker VM. But since port is published 0.0.0.0:5432 I expected host to reach it.

jake: Try `docker run --rm --network host alpine nc -zv localhost 5432`? (Note: mac doesn't support host networking for containers). Hmm. Another check: can other hosts on your network reach 5432? Probably not needed.

tori: I tried `curl http://localhost:5432` and got nothing (expected). However this morning I had Firewall enabled for 'Block all incoming connections' before disabling it — maybe Docker didn't update its socket. I restarted Docker Desktop and now localhost tcp connects! psql worked after restart.

nia: Nice. Restarting Docker Desktop is a great fallback. For the onboarding doc maybe we should add a line: "If published ports are unreachable on mac, try restarting Docker Desktop and ensure no other Postgres is installed."

tori: Also learned: libpq behavior — omitting host can try unix socket which won't work for container; always prefer `-h localhost` or PGHOST when pointing at container.

lee: Good write-up. Also mention colima vs docker desktop differences and the `network_mode` caveat.

jake: Quick tip for local dev: prefer using the app inside the compose network (service name: db:5432) to avoid host networking confusion.

tori: Thanks everyone — PR incoming to add these notes and a short checklist (restart Docker Desktop, check local Postgres, force TCP with -h localhost). Appreciate the warm welcome! :wave:
